chunks.title: Respond (CFTR) API Reference
chunks.text:
Respond (CFTR) API Reference cftr-api-reference

Cyware Fusion and Threat Response (CFTR) is a threat response automation platform that combines cyber fusion, advanced orchestration, and automation. Using the CFTR application security analysts can tackle all kinds of threats including malware, vulnerabilities, incidents, campaigns, and threat actors. Using the CFTR integrated threat databases, security analysts can manage and respond to all kinds of security threats such as malware, vulnerabilities, and threat actors.

CFTR API is organized around REST. You can use this API Reference to engage with the CFTR services programmatically and enable any automation or integration with other systems in your environment.

Note: You can make a maximum of 6000 API requests every 15 minutes to Respond.

Supported Version

Cyware Fusion and Threat Response (CFTR) v3.0 and higher.

chunks.title: Authentication
chunks.text:
Authentication cftr-api-reference > authentication

Mandatory Parameters in CFTR API calls

For any API URL request made to the CFTR application, you must include three mandatory parameters, namely Access ID, Expires, and Signature.

  • Access ID - Access ID is available to you when you generate API credentials from the CFTR application.
  • Expires - Expires indicates when this request expires. Use the below formula to make expires. Default margin for expiry is 20 seconds.
    expires = current time + 20 sec
  • Signature - Create a signature from Access ID, Secret Key, and Expires Time.

You can get the access ID and the secret key when you generate API credentials from the CFTR application.

Base URL

A base URL (base_url) is the consistent part of your web address for the CFTR application. https://example.com/cftrapi/ is an example of a Base URL.
